skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md.find: **Defaults for every `delegate_task` call.** `mode: "async"` (a steer or resume of a running child, a `t3_thread_send`, gets no `t3_thread_wait` either, because a waiting call holds your turn while other reports wait), full tool access (a read-only child gets "inspect only, change no file" in its brief), file pointers not inlined context, an explicit `target` per role (configurable via `/setup-pstack`. Role defaults in [Models](#models)). Code delegates tier by difficulty. The hardest changes (cross-cutting design, gnarly concurrency, subtle algorithms) go to your strongest judgment model (the `hardest tasks` default in [Models](#models)), whether the task needs judgment on vague intent or is a precisely specified sequence of steps to execute to the letter. Trivial mechanical edits go to your fast code model. Per-role lines in the model sheet that `/setup-pstack` writes override these defaults and the model choices in the routed skills (`how`, `why`, `arena`, `swarm`, `architect`, `interrogate`, `reflect`). A role with no line keeps its default, and a role line of `inherit-parent` or `auto` runs that role on the parent chat model (omit `target`). Each code playbook's configured model comes from its line (`feature, refactoring`, `bug-fix`, `perf-issue`, or `hillclimb`), and the hardest changes read `hardest tasks`. Prose and judgment read `judgment and prose`.
skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md.replace: **Do it yourself, or delegate.** Do the work in this chat when any of these holds: you can't write an acceptance command that fails on wrong work (judgment, a design choice, prose for the user, a call only the user can make); the brief would take longer than the work (one file, under about 15 minutes or 50 changed lines); the work needs context from this chat that isn't in a file yet; you are checking a child's result; or a child already failed the same task twice, so the third attempt is yours or a split into smaller tasks. Otherwise delegate, with a complete brief.

skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md.find: **Match the model to the job.** Before each spawn, start from the role's line or default and pick the reasoning level and speed the job needs. The `/setup-pstack` budget sets each role's starting level, xhigh by default. Raise it one step, up to max, for the hardest or subtlest work. Lower it one step for judgment and two or more steps for routine work. Use fast mode, the provider's speed option (`fastMode=true` on Claude, a fast `serviceTier` such as `priority` on Codex), only when the job is urgent, meaning CI or trunk is red or a person is blocked on the result right now. Otherwise use standard speed, the entry without that option. Verification is the exception and stays on the `swarm workers` model and speed (default in the **swarm** skill's Models section). Change only the entry's reasoning option (`effort` on Claude, `reasoningEffort` on Codex and Grok) and its speed option, and keep the family the role names, so a diverse panel stays diverse. If the model has no value at that level, or no speed option, use its nearest one in `orchestrator_capabilities`. A role on `auto` or `inherit-parent` stays on the parent model. If `delegate_task` rejects the adjusted entry, do not try another adjusted entry. Use the role's line or default and say so. If `delegate_task` rejects that too, continue with the calling skill's fallback. An entry counts as rejected once `delegate_task` fails on it with `model_unavailable` or `provider_unavailable`, or rejects its options. Never pass a rejected entry, and skip any fallback whose entry is already rejected. When the calling skill has no fallback, use the closest target of the role's family that `orchestrator_capabilities` lists, or omit `target` so the subagent runs on the parent model when it lists none. When the calling skill's fallback runs out of entries without saying what to do next, omit `target` too. Say so in both cases.
skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md.replace:
**Every brief follows `<plugin root>/skills/poteto-mode/brief.md`.** It has a header with the job type, size (S or M), time limit and disk limit, then Goal, Acceptance command, Files you may write, Non-goals, Context, Stop conditions and Report. For a complete brief, the child's extension enforces the file list, a write sandbox, the time and disk limits, and red before green, and appends a report block written from commands it ran. Check a result by running its acceptance command, `git status --porcelain` against the file list, and `du -sk` yourself. Never judge a result by rereading the work.

**Defaults for every `delegate_task` call.** `mode: "async"` (a steer or resume of a running child, a `t3_thread_send`, gets no `t3_thread_wait` either, because a waiting call holds your turn while other reports wait), full tool access (a read-only child gets "inspect only, change no file" in its brief), file pointers not inlined context, a `target` from `pstack_model` per job (see [Models](#models)). Code delegates tier by job type and size from the routing table: the hardest changes (cross-cutting design, gnarly concurrency, subtle algorithms) are job `hard`, and trivial mechanical edits are job `mechanical`. Per-role lines in the model sheet that `/setup-pstack` writes override these defaults and the model choices in the routed skills (`how`, `why`, `arena`, `swarm`, `architect`, `interrogate`, `reflect`). A role with no line keeps its default, and a role line of `inherit-parent` or `auto` runs that role on the parent chat model (omit `target`). Each code playbook's configured model comes from its line (`feature, refactoring`, `bug-fix`, `perf-issue`, or `hillclimb`), and the hardest changes read `hardest tasks`. Prose and judgment read `judgment and prose`.

**Match the model to the job.** Before each spawn, call `pstack_model` with the role, the job type and the size. The routing table picks the tier, model and reasoning, routes around accounts that are out of usage, and keeps a panel's families diverse. Verification stays on `swarm workers`. Treat the routing table as a default, and follow the user's model, reasoning, and speed choices when they differ.

| Job | S | M |
|---|---|---|
| mechanical: lint, rename, config, format | Haiku 5.5, low | Sonnet 5.5, medium |
| check: run given commands, report exit codes | GPT 6 Luna, low | Haiku 5.5, medium |
| research: writes one notes file | Muse Spark 1.3, medium | Muse Wonder 1.0, medium |
| implement: one unit with named tests | GPT 6.1 Sol, medium | Sonnet 5.5, high |
| hard: cross-cutting, concurrency, perf, unknown-cause bug | Opus 5.5, high | Opus 5.5, high |
| review panel | Opus 5.5, Muse Wonder Full 1.0, GPT 6.1 Sol, all high | same |
| design panel | Opus 5.5, Muse Wonder Full 1.0, GPT 6 Astra, all high | same |

Judgment and prose for the user stay in this chat. When a family is out of usage, the same tier in the next family takes the job, and GPT only ever takes size S work. When this chat's own model runs out, the extension asks T3 to resume this thread after the reset.

skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md.find: A child starts in your checkout, which suits one writer while you write nothing. A writer that runs beside other writers or your own edits gets `isolation: "worktree"`, and T3 gives it a new worktree and branch from your thread's checkout at its `HEAD` commit. Commit what it builds on first, because uncommitted edits stay behind. A child that must start from another commit, such as a PR head or fresh trunk, gets `isolation: "worktree"` even when it only reads. Its brief names that commit or ref, and before anything else the child runs `git fetch` and moves its own branch there with `git reset --hard`. T3 can rename that branch during the run, so the brief tells the child to end its reply with the output of `pwd`, `git branch --show-current`, and `git rev-parse HEAD`. After review, bring its commits onto your branch with `git merge <branch>`, which fast-forwards when your branch has not moved. A PR opens only from a T3 thread's branch, yours or that of a child that owns the PR. In a repo with no commit yet, `delegate_task` refuses the worktree with `Unable to resolve the parent checkout commit`, so commit first. When this thread's project is not a git checkout, which gets the same refusal, when your work lives in a checkout other than the one `t3_worktree_status` names, or when you copy uncommitted changes into the child's worktree, create that worktree with `git worktree add` from `HEAD` instead. Remove that worktree and its branch after the result. A child sent into a worktree it does not own, one you made this way or one a finished worker left, keeps `isolation: "shared"`. Its brief names that absolute path as the only place it writes, and tells it to run every command there (`workdir` on Codex) and to edit by absolute path. Record your own `git status --porcelain` before you dispatch a writer to another checkout, and check after the result that it is unchanged. A step a playbook says to delegate goes to `delegate_task` on that role's sheet entry, not into your own tool calls, unless you state a reason such as a step too small to brief. A research delegate no role names runs on the `how explorer` entry. A model's family is the first segment of its ID's last `/` part, such as `claude`, `gpt`, or `grok`, whatever provider instance serves it, and your own family is the one in `orchestrator_capabilities`' `inheritedModel`. A rejected target runs on another target of the same family from `orchestrator_capabilities`, and you say so. `orchestrator_capabilities` lists a short set of models per provider, and its `search` finds the others. A required review with no reviewer from another family stays `BLOCKED: independent review`.

skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md.find: Role defaults on T3, stamped from `plugins/pstack/models.json`. A role line in the model sheet overrides each one. The sheet is `~/.config/t3-pstack/models.md` (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/t3-pstack/models.md` when that is set), one per machine, and `/setup-pstack` writes it. When it is missing, read `t3-pstack-models.md` in the host's config directory (`$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `~/.claude` on Claude Code, `$CODEX_HOME` or `~/.codex` on Codex). An entry is `<providerInstanceId>/<modelId>` plus `<optionId>=<value>` pairs, and it maps onto `delegate_task`'s `target`, with the provider instance as `providerInstanceId`, the model as `model`, and the pairs as `options`. It splits at its first `/`, so a model ID with its own `/`, such as OpenCode's `<provider>/<model>`, is written whole after it. Option IDs differ per provider, so take them from `orchestrator_capabilities`. `inherit-parent` or `auto` omits `target`.
skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md.replace: Get every target from the `pstack_model` tool. Pass the role name, the job type and the size from the routing table under [Subagents](#subagents). Without a job, pass the complexity instead: `groundwork` for cheap mechanical work, `bounded` for involved but bounded work, `general` for work that needs substantial judgment. The tool reads the role's line in the model sheet (`~/.config/pi-t3-bridge/models.md`, written by `/setup-pstack`). A line naming a model is used as written, moved to a provider T3 can run right now when needed. When that line names no reasoning level, the job's complexity sets it, as for routed roles. A role with no line, or `inherit-parent` or `auto`, is routed by this extension's `models.json`: the parent's model family, sized and reasoned by complexity, and for panels one seat per family. Pass each returned target as `delegate_task`'s `target`. `inherit-parent` means omit `target`. `blocked` means the panel cannot reach two model families on this T3, so record its reason.

skills/poteto-mode/brief.md.replace:
- Every shell command runs in a sandbox, which is `sandbox-exec` on macOS and `bwrap` on Linux. The sandbox can write only to the workdir, its git directory, the tool caches, the pnpm store and the system temp folder, and it keeps the git hooks and git config read-only.
- A delegated child needs all seven sections of this template. If its brief misses one, the extension blocks every tool, and the parent has to send a complete brief.
- A bullet under "Files you may write" may list several paths. Every word with a slash or a glob counts as a path, e.g. `- packages/a/** and packages/b/c.ts`.
- The disk limit leaves out `node_modules`, because pnpm fills it from the store. Build output still counts.
- The child skips install scripts, so `pnpm install` and `npm install` run no `prepare` or `postinstall`. Don't ask for `prepare` to pass. If a postinstall generates files, e.g. `next typegen`, put the build or typecheck that generates them in the acceptance command.
- npm also skips the `pre` and `post` scripts of `npm run` and `npm test` in the child, so name them in the acceptance command, e.g. `npm run prebuild && npm test`.

When it is missing, read `t3-pstack-models.md` in the host's config directory (`$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `~/.claude` on Claude Code, `$CODEX_HOME` or `~/.codex` on Codex). An entry is `<providerInstanceId>/<modelId>` plus `<optionId>=<value>` pairs, and it maps onto `delegate_task`'s `target`, with the provider instance as `providerInstanceId`, the model as `model`, and the pairs as `options`. Pick each subagent's reasoning level and fast or standard speed for the job, per the Subagents section of the **poteto-mode** skill.

skills/arena/SKILL.md.find: After all Phase B candidates complete, choose one model from the `arena cross-judge pool` line in the model sheet. The judge is never from the parent's family, as Phase A step 3 defines families. Try only the entries from another family, in pool order. An `auto` or `inherit-parent` entry is the parent model, so it never judges. Among the entries from another family, try first those whose model ran fewer candidates, so no model scores its own work when another can judge. Pool order decides among entries that ran as many, and the reply says when the judge ran a candidate. With the default runners and pool in [Models](#models), a Claude parent skips the Claude entry and gets the next one, and a parent from any other family gets the Claude entry first. If `delegate_task` rejects an entry, use the same model at the closest reasoning level or speed that `orchestrator_capabilities` lists for it, under any provider instance, or move to the next entry when there is none. If no entry from another family runs, try the default pool's entries from another family the same way. If none of those runs, skip the judge, pick the base alone in Phase D, and say so. If `orchestrator_capabilities` names no `inheritedModel`, try the pool's targets in pool order and say that the family check did not run. The judge sees the rubric and the candidates by path label, scores each criterion, and recommends a base with rationale. It runs in parallel with your reading in Phase D. Don't spawn it while candidates are still writing.
